newsitem.title: USA: Iomega shares rise after earnings.
newsitem.headline: Iomega shares rise after earnings.

text.p: Iomega Corp shares rose as much as 9.3 percent in late morning trading Friday, a day after the disk-drive maker reported third-quarter earnings that were better than Wall Street expected.

Shares of Iomega, which makes removable disk drives, were up two at 24-7/8 on Nasdaq trading of 4.63 million shares, making it the most active issue on the exchange. Earlier, the shares traded as high as 25-57/64.

After the market closed yesterday, Iomega said its third quarter net income jumped six-fold to $12.8 million, or $0.09 a share, from $2.03 million, or $0.02, in the same quarter a year ago. Third quarter revenue more than tripled to $310.1 million from $84.7 million.
Wall Street expected Iomega, based in Roy, Utah, to earn $0.07, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.
Kim Edwards, Iomega's chief executive officer, had told analysts to expect a "challenging" third quarter because of weak personal computer sales in Europe.
Iomega, however, managed to sell more of its Zip, Jaz and Ditto disk drives than it had planned, particularly in the U.S., Edwards told analysts in a conference call yesterday.
"Their numbers were incredible" in the third quarter and Iomega probably will continue to do well in the fourth, said Howard Rosencrans, an analyst at H.D. Brous & Co in Great Neck, N.Y.

Iomega makes disk drives that use disks similar to floppies, but with many more times the capacity. In recent months, Iomega has been winning contracts from PC manufacturers who want to include its drives with their machines.
